title: Swap Stability in Schelling Games on Graphs
reasoning: The paper is a game-theoretic study of social segregation models. While it mentions religion as one of several factors (along with politics and socioeconomic status) that influence human residential segregation, it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, morals, or ethics. It focuses on the mathematical properties of swap-based stability, social welfare, and diversity indices in a graph-based game.
